copy.linkedin:
p(Doom)1 v0.14.0 shipped today, and the interesting part isn't a feature.

The historical event deck was retimed so one turn is one month. That changes which events fire on a given seed - which means a score from last week and a score from tomorrow are measuring different games. Most projects would ship that quietly and let the leaderboard keep adding them together.

Instead the ladder forks. Old entries stay valid and visible on the old epoch; new runs go to a new one; the two are never merged. The board's identity includes which ruleset produced it, so a rules change can't silently invalidate a record.

It cost a release to build that and it will keep costing. It's worth it, because the alternative is a number that looks authoritative and isn't.

Also in there: a claim-a-name prompt so the board isn't fifty identical default names, and a failed leaderboard fetch that is now visible rather than silent - because silent failure and nobody-is-playing look identical from the outside.

Still an alpha. Free, open source, non-commercial.
